title: Stay safe when connecting to Wi-Fi on the go

body_markdown:
Keeping your devices connected while traveling can be a challenge. While a 5G network can be a great way to maintain internet access on your phone, it may not be the best option for other devices.


Wi-Fi provides a strong, reliable connection on the go – but not all networks are safe to join. Whether you’re at the airport, train station, hotel, or a family member’s home, it’s important to take precautions. Malicious hotspots can look nearly identical to legitimate networks and may allow criminals to steal your online data.


During the busy holiday travel season, here are some tips to keep your devices and your information protected while using public Wi-Fi.


#### Join the correct network


This may sound like an obvious piece of advice, but if you open your settings and see multiple variations of a similar network name, this could be an attempt at a “man-in-the-middle” attack.


That’s


a tactic that scammers use to get you to log on to their network and enter your information. PC Mag recommends taking the time to ask an employee to


identify


the real network for that location.


Be sure to confirm the exact network name and


password, and


avoid networks that


don’t


require a password.


#### Use a VPN


A


virtual private network, or VPN,


is a tool that you can


install on your device


to keep


connections between you and the websites you visit private.


Acco


rding to Tech Radar, even the most affordable VPNs can


provide features that will ward off internet intruders


and make your online activity difficult to trace.


Choose a reputable provider and be cautious with free VPNs, which may collect or sell your data.


Researching VPNs and installing one that works for you is


a good step to take before traveling.


*Note: TDS customers should check out the [TDS Internet Security Suite](https://tdstelecom.com/shop/internet-services/enhancements/home-internet-security.html) , which includes a VPN!*


#### Don’t access sensitive personal information on a public network


It may be safe to browse the news or stream videos while on a public network, but the National Cybersecurity Alliance recommends staying away from more sensitive websites like online banking and avoiding inputting personal data or credit card information on public Wi-Fi.


If you need to handle something sensitive, use your


phone’s hotspot instead, and turn on multi-factor authentication for your email, banking, and social


accounts


so a captured password


isn’t


enough to get in.


#### Check for “HTTPS” in the website address


Another tip for using public Wi-Fi is to keep an eye on the website details in the address bar at the top of your browser.


The prefix “HTTPS” means


the connection to


that website


is encrypted, though


scam


sites can use


it


too, so also double-check that the


site


address is spelled correctly.


Experts at Norton 360 say that if a website is lacking that “S” and just reads “HTTP,” your online activity may be visible to anyone else on the network.


#### Stay on top of software updates


The team at Norton 360 also


advises


keeping your devices up to date on the latest versions of software. Updates often provide crucial fixes to vulnerabilities to protect your devices from hackers and data breaches, so be sure to complete all updates before heading out on a trip.


Turning on automatic updates helps make sure you


don’t


miss any


.


#### Turn off auto-connect and file sharing


Devices that automatically rejoin saved networks can connect to a look-alike hotspot without you noticing.


Turn off auto-connect,


Airdrop


or file sharing, and Bluetooth discoverability while


you’re


out, keep your


firewall


and screen lock on, and “forget” public networks once you leave.


The National Cybersecurity Alliance has a


[detailed list of tips and resources](https://www.staysafeonline.org/articles/public-computers-and-public-wi-fi-how-to-stay-safe-out-and-about) to stay secure online while traveling.


Cyber threats


won’t


take the holidays off, so stay prepared and vigilant wherever you roam this year.
